judgments.reasoning_cat1: A possession test tied to a fixed dollar amount plus the vague rider "and otherwise reasonably acceptable to Lender."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It repeats the Section 3.1(t) package and overlaps with Section 4.2's delivery duty and Section 8.17's cure mechanism, which are consistent but layered.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires a "current" Borrowing Base Certificate without defining currency, and the certificate's form is left to be supplied later.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit B-2 is a placeholder and Section 6.2 sets its own delivery timetable (each Advance and monthly), so the content of this condition depends on documents outside the executed text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed three-year term, followed by a right to terminate "immediately and without notice" that is nonetheless "subject to any notice and cure rights otherwise provided by this Agreement" — the two halves of the sentence pull against each other.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.1(c) also allows termination on an Event of Default and Section 8.2 supplies cure periods, so the interplay of immediate termination and cure rights must be worked out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision is a placeholder, but it is numbered "3.4" in the text, duplicating the preceding Term section's number.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section headings and numbers are declared to be for convenience only by Section 16.2, which blunts the effect of the duplication.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear statement that all Obligations accelerate on termination and that Liens survive until payment in full and commitments end.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coordinates with Sections 3.4, 3.7 and the cash-collateralization concept in the Section 1.4 "repayment in full" gloss; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite 30-day notice and pay-off mechanic, with the premium expressly required.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because the Applicable Prepayment Premium is zero after the first anniversary, the premium requirement becomes formal only, a coherent if odd result.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A liquidated-damages recital covering four very different termination events, including foreclosure and plan confirmation, with the premium payable only "if applicable" — an ambiguity about when it is applicable at all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with the Applicable Prepayment Premium definition (zero after year one) and Section 3.6's automatic acceleration, the clause may have no operative content after the first anniversary.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional grant of security interest, closing with a flat prohibition: "except for Permitted Dispositions, Borrowers ... shall have no authority, express or implied, to dispose of any item or portion of the Collateral."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That prohibition makes the Permitted Dispositions definition and the release mechanics in Section 4.9(b) the only exit from the collateral pool, so a dispute over a sale of Notes Receivable would be decided by reading these provisions together with Sections 7.3(c) and 7.4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires endorsement and delivery of Notes Receivable, sets a $250,000,000 floor with the soft rider "otherwise reasonably acceptable to Lender," and the final sentence reads "If Event of Default has occurred," dropping the article.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interlocks with Sections 3.1(t), 3.3(e), 6.16 and 8.17, and with Section 4.9's release mechanics that take notes back out of Lender's possession.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Post-default collection rights stated in three concrete alternatives, plus a trust obligation over Collections.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Overlaps with Sections 4.8, 9.1(d)-(e) and 2.6, which grant similar rights on similar triggers; the arrangement is cumulative rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard financing statement authorization and ratification.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the Filing Authorization Letter definition and Section 3.1(a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three-Business-Day notification and assignment duty for commercial tort claims; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Borrower Collateral clause (c) and Schedule 5.7(d).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An open-ended "any and all" further-assurances obligation with a self-execution authorization, plus a detailed copyright-registration proviso; the breadth of "Additional Documents" is bounded only by Lender's Permitted Discretion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with Sections 4.4(a) and 4.5's power of attorney, which expressly backstops a refusal to sign; internally consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Assignment of storage access rights exercisable only after an Event of Default; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 5.5's public warehouse proviso and Section 7.15.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad irrevocable power of attorney, but each of the six powers is separately delimited and most are conditioned on a continuing Event of Default.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Clause (a) ties to Section 4.4 and the rest to Sections 4.3 and 9.1, coherently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Inspection and verification rights limited to normal business hours and reasonable notice; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 6.1, 6.5(c) and the audit fee provision in Section 2.10(d).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires "reasonable steps" toward control and permits liquidation of accounts; the operative trigger is stated clearly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The liquidation right arises on "a Default or Event of Default," a lower trigger than the Event of Default standard used in Sections 4.3, 4.5 and 9.1, an inconsistency in remedies triggers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Borrowers may take such action on the Notes Receivable "as the Borrowers may deem advisable" and grant any adjustment "to which such maker may be lawfully entitled" — subjective and open standards governing the servicing of the core collateral.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Revocation is tied to "the terms of the Servicing Agreement," an extrinsic document, and the same subject matter is addressed by Sections 6.5, 9.1(e) and 9.1(o), which give Lender overlapping and differently worded rights.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Return of a repaid note "to facilitate its payment" and release of Liens "promptly upon receipt of the final payment" — the sequence is slightly circular (return before payment, release after).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits with Section 4.2's delivery requirement and Section 8.17's $250,000,000 floor, since releases can erode the delivered pool.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The release is conditioned on the note being "sold by Fund in accordance with the terms of this Agreement" and the transfer is made "against payment of the agreed amount therefor" — neither the compliance condition nor the "agreed amount" is spelled out here, so the trigger and the price are both left to other provisions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Whether a sale complies depends on Permitted Dispositions clause (e) (a price floor tied to unpaid balance) and on Section 2.6(a)(iii)'s requirement that proceeds be paid directly into a Cash Management Account, while Section 4.1 bars any other disposition; reconciling those is precisely the kind of dispute this clause invites.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three concrete triggers for a reassignment, on forms prepared by Administrative Borrower and reasonably acceptable to Lender.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 6.16's recording obligation and Sections 4.9(a)-(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bring-down and survival lead-in qualified by "in all material respects"; conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Section 3.3(a) and the Compliance Certificate; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Uses the archaic phrase "good and indefeasible title" for personal property and "good and marketable title" for real property, but the meaning is settled enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subject to Permitted Liens, which is coordinated with Section 7.2 and Schedule P-1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (i) warrants that each eligible note is secured by property "on which a commercial or residential development is located or is expected to be built" — "expected to be built" has no ascertainable boundary, and clause (b) warrants the absence of defenses only so far as "known."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: These representations are incorporated by reference into the Eligible Notes Receivable definition itself, so a breach here silently shrinks the Borrowing Base; the interaction with clauses (a)-(s) of that definition is dense.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Warrants that forms are "commensurate with forms and documentation used by prudent lenders in the same or similar circumstances" — a vague comparative standard — and then warrants unqualified compliance of all offering materials and "all aspects of Borrowers' operations" with all laws.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The unqualified securities-law warranty sits against Section 3.1(q)'s proviso allowing "reasonable assurances" to satisfy the same subject as a closing condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line representation that Equipment is fit for its purpose.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Equipment definition and Section 6.6.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Location representation with a proviso permitting loan files without original notes or lien instruments to sit in a public warehouse; clear enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The identical proviso appears in Section 7.15 and Section 6.9 permits schedule amendment, all coordinated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short representation about record-keeping.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 6.1's covenant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Schedule-referential statement of fact.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedule 5.7(a) states California for both Borrowers and no subsidiaries; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Schedule-referential statement of fact.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.9 permits amendment of the schedule on notice, consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Schedule-referential statement of fact.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.5 restricts changes to those numbers; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Closing-date representation about tort claims.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.4(b) covers after-acquired claims, and Schedule 5.7(d) says none; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard organization and qualification representation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Sections 3.1(e)-(f) and 6.12.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A representation about capitalization that carves out anything described "in an Offering Circular," an elastic and continuously changing document.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The parenthetical "(as updated from time to time)" conflicts with Section 6.14's statement that disclosure updates do not amend the Schedules, a real internal inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires a complete list of Subsidiaries "as updated from time to time"; the underlying "Subsidiary" definition excludes several kinds of controlled entities.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.14 says no notification amends the Schedules, and Section 7.13 forbids forming Subsidiaries at all, so a self-updating schedule of Subsidiaries is hard to reconcile.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Negative representation about options and warrants in Subsidiaries, with an Offering Circular carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Same self-updating schedule tension with Section 6.14; otherwise consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate due authorization representation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Section 3.1(c)'s resolutions condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A four-limb no-conflict representation qualified by "material contractual obligation," a familiar materiality filter.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 8.9's cross-default and Permitted Liens.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: No-consent representation with a filings carve-out; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 3.1(q)'s licenses condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard enforceability representation with an equitable-principles exception.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 8.16's Event of Default for contesting validity.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Flatly warrants that the Lender's Liens are "validly created, perfected, and first priority," a present-tense absolute given at signing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Perfection depends on filings and recordings still to be made under Sections 3.1(a), 4.4 and 6.16, and Section 8.14 treats a failure of perfection as a default, so the absolute warranty is in tension with the process the Agreement itself prescribes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Litigation representation with layered exclusions, including matters that "reasonably could not be expected to result in a Material Adverse Change" and routine Account Debtor enforcement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedule 5.10 discloses the Queen Mary and Harmony Holding matters; Section 6.3(g) requires ongoing notice, consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Combines a GAAP/fair-presentation warranty with a no-Material-Adverse-Change statement; the latter depends on the vague defined term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.3(d) and 6.3's reporting regime.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line solvency representation whose entire content comes from the truncated "Solvent" definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with Section 5.12(b)'s no-intent-to-hinder representation and Section 16.7's revival clause, this is the provision a later insolvency dispute would target, and the definition's single-limb test is where it would turn.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Denies any intent to hinder, delay or defraud creditors in connection with the transactions; a statement of intent rather than fact, but conventionally worded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paired with Section 5.12(a) and Section 16.7, which anticipates that transfers may nonetheless be avoided.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Simple negative representation about Benefit Plans.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Benefit Plan and ERISA Affiliate definitions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four knowledge-qualified environmental representations; conventional and bounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 6.13's covenant and Section 11.3(c)'s indemnity.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short, absolute no-broker representation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Ownership and listing representation with a materiality qualifier on the schedule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The "as updated from time to time" parenthetical again cuts against Section 6.14's no-amendment sentence; Schedule 5.16 says "None."

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Peaceful-possession lease representation limited to material leases; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 6.6 and 6.11.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires a listing of all Deposit and Securities Accounts; definite in requirement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedule 5.18 lists Greater Bay accounts while Section 2.6(a) requires Wells Fargo to be the sole Cash Management Bank after 60 days and Section 6.12(d) forbids other accounts, so the disclosed facts and the covenants pull apart.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The "taken as a whole" qualifier appears three times and the warranty covers all future information as well, which softens what would otherwise be a hard accuracy standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.14 requires prompt correction but says correction does not cure the prior misstatement, and Section 8.11 makes any material misstatement a default; the pieces fit together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires a "true and complete summary" of outstanding interests and debt "as is satisfactory to Lender"; the satisfaction rider is odd in a representation but harmless.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedule 5.20 cross-refers to Schedule 5.8 and lists the Fremont Bank loan, which matches Schedule P-1 and Section 7.1(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Representation about the title company list and their non-affiliation; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the Approved Title Insurance Company definition and Schedule 5.21.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A covenant lead-in running "so long as any credit hereunder shall be available and until payment in full of the Obligations," which is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The parallel Section 7 lead-in adds "until termination of this Agreement," a small drafting divergence between the affirmative and negative covenant packages.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires a GAAP-capable accounting system and a reporting system for Notes Receivable; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 6.2 and 6.3 and with Section 8.2(a)'s no-cure default treatment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A reporting table whose column structure is badly garbled in the text, and item (h) is an unlimited catch-all ("such other reports ... as Lender may request") appended to seven specific reports.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Failure to comply is an immediate Event of Default under Section 8.2(a) with no cure period, which makes the open-ended catch-all consequential.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed reporting deadlines; the phrase "within 30 days after the end of each month during each year" is clumsy and clause (d)(i) requires SEC-style reports "if applicable" to a private LLC.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to Sections 7.16 and 7.17 for compliance certification, and Section 7.10 conditions distributions on delivery of "the financial statements required by Section 6.3(b)," tying quarterly reporting to permitted payments.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A blank placeholder with no content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.2 does not list 6.4, so the blank causes no default-trigger problem (unlike the listing of 6.15).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The covenant to collect uses "commercially reasonable" three times in one sentence and adds a hold-harmless obligation, which is dense but intelligible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is expressly "[s]ubject to Section 4.8," which allocates servicing to Borrowers or Servicer, and overlaps with Section 9.1(e)/(o) after default.
